sections.question: Among the defendants in eight federal rulings of September 11-15, 2026, which, if any, had asked the court to dismiss on forum non conveniens grounds but were dismissed from the case on a different ground instead? Where two or more qualify, name them in any order.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Doc 7 (4chan and Lolcow v. Ofcom, D.D.C., September 15, 2026): Ofcom asked the court to dismiss on forum non conveniens and international comity grounds as well as on foreign sovereign immunity. The court addressed only immunity and dismissed the complaint for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction. Ofcom qualifies.

Step 2. Doc 1 (Advanced Technology Products v. Oriental Export Corporation, S.D. Ohio, September 11, 2026): one Motion to Dismiss was filed by both Oriental Export Corporation (OEC India) and OEC USA, Inc., and the Defendants moved to dismiss under Rules 12(b)(2) and 12(b)(6) "as well as the doctrine of forum non conveniens". The court granted OEC USA's request for dismissal under Rule 12(b)(2) and dismissed OEC USA without prejudice for lack of personal jurisdiction, so it never reached forum non conveniens for OEC USA. OEC USA qualifies.

Step 3. Exclusions. Doc 1: the same motion's forum non conveniens and personal-jurisdiction requests were denied as to OEC India, and only Count IX was dismissed, so OEC India stays in the case on Counts I to VIII. Doc 5: Royal Caribbean asked for forum non conveniens dismissal and was dismissed on exactly that ground. Doc 4: the Kansas defendants moved to transfer, not to dismiss, and DUAL's Rule 12(b)(6) motion was denied. In Doc 2, Doc 3, Doc 6 and Doc 8 no defendant asked for forum non conveniens dismissal; the doctrine appears only in a plaintiffs' waiver or in cited precedent.

Answer: Ofcom and OEC USA.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Look-alike company
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list
Where the trap sits: Doc 1, the Ohio ruling on the air-brake tubing dispute. Its forum non conveniens part speaks only of the Indian parent: "OEC India has not carried its ultimate burden to show that forum non conveniens dismissal is warranted", and its conclusion reads "The Motion is DENIED as to OEC India’s request for dismissal under the doctrine of forum non conveniens." The similarly named Delaware subsidiary, OEC USA, Inc., appears in that part only as already gone. Its role as a movant is shown elsewhere: the opening sentence says the Motion to Dismiss was "filed by Defendants Oriental Export Corporation (“OEC India”) and OEC USA, Inc.", and the procedural history says "Defendants now move to dismiss ATP’s Complaint under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 12(b)(2) and 12(b)(6), as well as the doctrine of forum non conveniens."
The wrong answer a careless solver gives: "Ofcom". The solver takes OEC India as the only company in the tubing case that sought forum non conveniens dismissal, sees that OEC India was not dismissed, and drops the tubing case, leaving only the regulator from the 4chan and Lolcow suit.
Why the correct answer avoids it: The careful reader asks who filed the motion whose forum non conveniens request the court decided. Both OEC companies filed that one motion, and the court rules on it as "Defendants’ Motion", so OEC USA asked for forum non conveniens dismissal too. The court then granted "OEC USA’s request for dismissal under Rule 12(b)(2)" and dismissed OEC USA without prejudice, a personal-jurisdiction ground, so OEC USA belongs beside Ofcom.

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Part vs total
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise
Where the trap sits: Doc 1, the conclusion of the Ohio ruling: "The Motion is GRANTED as to OEC India’s request for dismissal under Rule 12(b)(6) of ATP’s fraudulent inducement claim (Count IX), and that claim is DISMISSED." The next sentence also dismisses Counts I, III, V and VII "insofar as they seek damages or remedies beyond" the Section 13 limit. Both sentences put the word DISMISSED beside OEC India, the company whose forum non conveniens request the court denied.
The wrong answer a careless solver gives: "Ofcom, OEC USA and OEC India". The solver reads the Rule 12(b)(6) grant and the word DISMISSED as OEC India being dismissed on a ground other than forum non conveniens, and adds the parent company to the two correct defendants.
Why the correct answer avoids it: The question asks which movants were dismissed from the case. The same conclusion denies the motion as to the breach-of-contract, express-warranty and implied-warranty claims (Counts I to VIII), and denies OEC India's personal-jurisdiction and forum non conveniens requests. OEC India therefore remains a defendant facing eight counts; only one claim and part of the remedy were removed, so it stays out of the answer.
